title: Seamless Optical Illusion Fabric Design
content:
I’m excited to share one of my latest fabric designs — a seamless, high-gloss stretch material with a bold optical illusion print. The wavy lines in red, cyan, yellow, and white move fluidly over a black base, creating a dynamic, colorful effect that shifts beautifully with movement and light.

![cacf8e7292664679ba70ce95c824bbba](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/765395c5a68a45f391b3b0c4e5b8256f/images/cacf8e7292664679ba70ce95c824bbbamaterial%20preview%202_1.png)

This fabric isn’t just about the look. The seamless print means there are no visible breaks or repetitions, making it perfect for designs that need a clean, continuous flow — whether in digital fashion, activewear, or stage costumes. The stretch performance and glossy finish add an extra layer of depth and shine, making every piece stand out.

![b2f6a590072442ffb7efa333c623e1c4](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/765395c5a68a45f391b3b0c4e5b8256f/images/b2f6a590072442ffb7efa333c623e1c4set%20top%20cut_1.png)

🧵 Material details:

• Seamless chromatic print (no visible pattern breaks)

• High-gloss, stretch performance fabric

• Smooth, second-skin feel

• Digital print with layered chromatic edge effect

• Great for activewear, avatar clothing, 3D fashion, and statement pieces

✨ I designed this material for creators who want something vibrant and flexible — a fabric that works as well in motion as it does in static designs.

![72799a438a4043779dc3e1ae9e9bfa17](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/765395c5a68a45f391b3b0c4e5b8256f/images/72799a438a4043779dc3e1ae9e9bfa17material%20preview%201_1.png)

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/765395c5a68a45f391b3b0c4e5b8256f/images/9cbd12468781469f82ee03e1c7940058material%20preview%20o_3.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/765395c5a68a45f391b3b0c4e5b8256f/images/2645de3681f040928ab83a95c06edac8tumbnail.png)

content_description: Showcasing a vibrant, seamless high-gloss stretch fabric with a bold optical illusion print designed for dynamic, flawless fashion and digital creations.

title: MD Problem with lastest update USD Graphics not visible
content:
Hi, after the last update(2025.0.243) I'm having issues exporting to USD from Marvelous Designer. I had a project with some graphics, and when I'm trying to export them to USD(no UV grouping) all my graphics are lost. I thougt it was an Issue on the imported program but it seems that is an issue that the graphics are not visible, but they are present. I used Omniverse USD Viewer to confirm this

On a previous project taht I had the USD version I also tested and the same issue, in this version graphics are removed.

I need them exporting on NON UV grouping.

![9012d2ededf34c44aef385eda89fccfa](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/504b6655816b408d8e466b2a9bd12920/images/9012d2ededf34c44aef385eda89fccfaimage.png)![1aacfabafd594225a63d9364346b1e28](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/504b6655816b408d8e466b2a9bd12920/images/1aacfabafd594225a63d9364346b1e28image.png)

title: Red circle in LiveSync no matter what
content:
Hi all,

I'm trying to use LiveSync but it doesn't work. I have Marvelous Designer (2025.0.243) open, and I have the LiveSync installed in UE5.6.0 - and I also have Substance 3d plugin installed.

I have a garment open in Marvelous - and the only help that seems to exist on this topic is to "select a fabric" and then "restart unreal and marvelous designer" if it doesn't work.

![f34f2c34aa464d89b188618a97e0a21a](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/99fdf6c7d4b64db09982347c211846d8/images/f34f2c34aa464d89b188618a97e0a21aredcircle_nomatterwhat.jpg)

Does anyone have any more problem solving solutions??

I have Norton anti-virus installed, and I've made a rule for that to allow all connections with MARVELOUS DESIGNER, but it doesn't list anything when I try to add LiveSync.

toby

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Hi mrtobycook,Have you enabled the LiveSyng setting in Marvelous Designer? It's a new setting introduced in Marvelous Designer 2025.0.243, designed to ensure a more stable connection after we performed some code-level cleanup. You can find the setting by navigating to Preferences > Other > LiveSync. For more details, please take a look at the relevant documentation: https://connect.clo-set.com/community/post/99fdf6c7d4b64db09982347c211846d8 me know if this works! 🙂Best regards,Bryan
Reply 1: No I hadn't. Thanks Bryan :-)
content_description: A troubleshooting and support page for resolving LiveSync connection issues between Marvelous Designer, Unreal Engine 5.6, and Substance 3D plugins.

title: XIII - Hard Surface Modeling with Marvelous Designer
content:
## _Eugene Lemeshko used Marvelous Designer in an unconventional way to create XIII, a gothic armor piece inspired by medieval history and tarot symbolism. His workflow showcases the software’s surprising flexibility for hard surface modeling, especially in AR design._

* * *

![7b26fb7552d04d0a9721c129286d88c3](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/56b5c3e48b604892aa12dcbb91bea45d/images/7b26fb7552d04d0a9721c129286d88c3logo.png)

# **Interview with**[**Eugene Lemeshko**](https://www.artstation.com/artwork/mA0a9y)**| XIII | 3D Character/Cloth/Armor Artist**

# **Introducing the Artist – Can you share a bit about yourself and your project, XIII?**

![1abe1192b8cc45b5b635020d9d7fd4a9](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/56b5c3e48b604892aa12dcbb91bea45d/images/1abe1192b8cc45b5b635020d9d7fd4a9main.png)![d20b77d6a0034d729ccdd8cd104c5a74](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/56b5c3e48b604892aa12dcbb91bea45d/images/d20b77d6a0034d729ccdd8cd104c5a74mood.png)

My name is Evgenii, and I’m a 3D artist with over four years of experience creating 3D assets and digital garments for AR platforms - including Instagram filters and digital clothing for Snapchat. Also, I am an award winner in several contests from Meta Inc. and Snapchat, including these contests ([Link 1,](https://blog.lenslist.co/2022/09/27/lenslist-x-snapchat-ar-fashion-month-challenge-winners-announcement/) [Link 2](https://blog.lenslist.co/2021/12/09/winners-announcement-2-c4c-our-future-planet/))

For a long time, I worked as a 3D designer at ZERO10, where we focused on creating ultra-realistic digital twins of real-life garments and accessories. (I also [contributed to asset creation and optimization for a collaboration between CLO and Stanford University.](https://www.instagram.com/reel/CspKTB3AwbD/?utm_source=ig_web_copy_link&igsh=MzRlODBiNWFlZA%3D%3D))

My background is quite unique - I previously worked in the tourism industry and spent over ten years involved in historical reenactment of the High Middle Ages (14th–15th centuries). That experience deeply influenced my personal style and love for all things medieval: armor, weapons, culture, and history. One day, in my free time, I wondered - **could I create armor in Marvelous Designer?**

That’s how the project XIII was born - a representation of the "Death" card from the Rider-White Tarot deck, visualized as a black gothic armor with golden elements that echoes medieval aesthetics. I originally created this armor as a personal project during my time at ZERO10. There were specific limitations - the entire model had to be under 10,000 vertices, meaning all the armor had to share a single UV map, one material, one mesh, and all the intricate details had to be hand-painted into the textures.

Final result for AR Try-On is [here](https://zero10.ar/garment/eugencolter-xiii).

# **You designed most of your armor pieces using Marvelous Designer, which is quite unique. What was it like working with hard surface modeling in this software?**

![d7854f9180bc437c865234263a8c6eba](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/56b5c3e48b604892aa12dcbb91bea45d/images/d7854f9180bc437c865234263a8c6ebaclose3.png)![cf640b1a28fc4b1aae44f4cdc6bd2bcc](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/56b5c3e48b604892aa12dcbb91bea45d/images/cf640b1a28fc4b1aae44f4cdc6bd2bccclose2.png)![ae5ce539b8c2429885874f900b960452](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/56b5c3e48b604892aa12dcbb91bea45d/images/ae5ce539b8c2429885874f900b960452close1.png)

The idea to create armor in Marvelous Designer started as a spontaneous experiment. Honestly, I didn’t expect much from it at first. I had tried to make armor before, but it always looked too soft or plush like [this](https://zero10.ar/garment/eugencolter-iron-maiden). However, Marvelous Designer has a huge advantage - it lets you work with patterns, much like real-life armorers do. Blacksmiths often use templates just like tailors - the only difference is that metal can be shaped and forged into rigid forms. Marvelous Designer offers a similar flexibility: you create a base pattern, simulate it to get the right shape, freeze it, and then gradually add more details. The key is controlling the deformation of each piece and using pins to lock certain parts together when needed.

# **Could you give us a brief rundown of the tools and software you used throughout your workflow?**

The main armor — everything except the helmet and gloves — was created entirely in Marvelous Designer. For the helmet and gloves, I used free assets as a base and rebuilt them from scratch in Blender. The sword and shield were also modeled in Blender. I refined the details in ZBrush and did all the texturing in Substance Painter. I created turntables in Blender, and the final renders were done in Marmoset Toolbag.

# ![9ab0379bb6bc4c14ac400858115d9939](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/56b5c3e48b604892aa12dcbb91bea45d/images/9ab0379bb6bc4c14ac400858115d9939orto.png)![366fe04785e1499abf3a5713286c08a3](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/56b5c3e48b604892aa12dcbb91bea45d/images/366fe04785e1499abf3a5713286c08a3weapon.png)**What were some of the biggest challenges you faced while working on this project?**

Marvelous Designer isn’t built for hard surface modeling, so getting the right shapes for armor was possible - but tricky. Every piece had to be carefully simulated, frozen, reinforced, and sometimes simulated again. Another important factor was adjusting seam angles - they play a huge role in creating bulges or indentations. One of the biggest challenges was the engraving. I had to manually paint all of it onto the curvature map in Photoshop to place it perfectly in UV space. It was a very meticulous process, but it helped preserve the clean topology I needed for the project.

# **Do you have any advice for artists looking to use Marvelous Designer for hard surface modeling?**

It’s absolutely doable - you can achieve almost any hard shape as long as you understand the basics of simulation and pattern freezing. But to be fair to the community: Marvelous is best suited for rigid but organic forms. If you want to create sleek, flowing, or surreal armor, Marvelous can be a great fit. However, if you're aiming to recreate historically accurate pieces and you're working under production deadlines, it might be more efficient to stick to classic modeling tools. That said - don’t be afraid to experiment. You never know what creative results might come from trying something unconventional.

# **How would you describe your overall experience working with Marvelous Designer?**

Out of all the clothing simulation tools I’ve tried, Marvelous Designer is the most intuitive and user-friendly — especially thanks to its clean interface. You can learn the basics and navigation within a few hours.

The new GPU-based rendering also speeds up the workflow significantly and allows for quicker prototyping and iteration. I would also like to share other projects that were created specifically for AR, which were also created using Marvelous Designer, as a tool of my pipeline: [example 1](https://www.artstation.com/artwork/GvdAna) / [example 2](https://www.artstation.com/artwork/2BZNex) / [example 3](https://www.artstation.com/artwork/4NlgDl).
content_description: Showcasing Eugene Lemeshko’s innovative use of Marvelous Designer to create the gothic XIII armor, blending medieval history and tarot symbolism with hard surface modeling techniques for AR design.

title: Meet the Winner: Creator's contest 2025 Vol.1 - Seifuku Decoded (Community's Choice, Dollfication)
content:
## ![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/2983c95760f941d7a11113b5305f38ed/images/1aac75e12cbf4002ad43d7dc111cb9febede2f3df6794fc2a130512b4d1262b5%E1%84%80%E1%85%B3%E1%84%85%E1%85%B5%E1%86%B75.jpg)_Fashion doll designer and fashion design student_[** _Dollfication_**](https://connect.clo-set.com/portfolio/387727/collection/collections) _captured the community’s heart with her pastel-toned reinterpretation of late '90s Gyaru style, earning her the_** _Community Choice Award_** _in the Marvelous Designer Creator’s Contest 2025. Step into the bold, adorable world of_[** _Dollfication_**](https://connect.clo-set.com/portfolio/387727/collection/collections) _💖✨_

![bede2f3df6794fc2a130512b4d1262b5](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/2983c95760f941d7a11113b5305f38ed/images/bede2f3df6794fc2a130512b4d1262b5%E1%84%80%E1%85%B3%E1%84%85%E1%85%B5%E1%86%B75.jpg)

# **Artist Introduction: please tell us about yourself.**

Hello Hello, I go online by Dollfication, I am a Fashion design student in my last semester and a full-time freelancer specifically as a fashion doll designer. My main motivation to join this contest was because the theme interested me but also because I have been having fascination with Japanese fashion and street style since decades. I even created in my second semester a winter Kogal inspired collection. So, it all seemed like the perfect time and the perfect place to be a destiny if you will and therefore, I had to participate in this contest.

# **We’d like to hear more about the art direction in your Creator’s contest 2025 Vol.1 Seifuku Decoded Contest. What was the visual style you were aiming for?**

The main visual style that I was aiming for was a classic early late 90’s/00’s kogal Gyaru look with a pastel themed color palette I also wanted the overall look and fantasy to be very cute and doll-like even cartoonish. Animes like “My Dress-Up Darling” or “SuperGals” were definitely also a huge inspiration for the overall look.

# **Would you be able to give us a quick overview of the different tools you use in your pipeline with a focus on Marvelous Designer? Have you encountered any challenges and how have you overcome them?**

The base avatar that I used was a CLO “Jinny” avatar however I did modified it in some way or another buy giving it a different more tanned skin tone compared to the original pale skin tone and changing the eye color as well as completely changing the makeup look overall to a more Gyaru late 90’s/early 00’s makeup. The Outfit was created using both mix of CLO and Marvelous Designer. I also created a custom repeat pattern for the skirt and bow using procreate and photoshop.

![4bc56fa5c4094829b45e1d4c07162b63](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/2983c95760f941d7a11113b5305f38ed/images/4bc56fa5c4094829b45e1d4c07162b63%E1%84%80%E1%85%B3%E1%84%85%E1%85%B5%E1%86%B71.jpg)![c0ff4aa9ad3d48b58e0ef8444c8c0ba0](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/2983c95760f941d7a11113b5305f38ed/images/c0ff4aa9ad3d48b58e0ef8444c8c0ba0%E1%84%80%E1%85%B3%E1%84%85%E1%85%B5%E1%86%B72.jpg)

# **Are there any tips and tricks with Marvelous Designer that you can share with the community?**

Honestly just experiment and see what works for you best, Its all about creating a workflow that suits your needs, learn by trying and testing, cut and transform a basic starter shirt in CLO/Marvelous Designer and enjoy the journey of learning! ♡

![5783ab9f1c63423f81d7e7e1175d396a](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/2983c95760f941d7a11113b5305f38ed/images/5783ab9f1c63423f81d7e7e1175d396a%E1%84%80%E1%85%B3%E1%84%85%E1%85%B5%E1%86%B74.jpg)![9e86181ea90c4d389562d2da8f1699cb](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/2983c95760f941d7a11113b5305f38ed/images/9e86181ea90c4d389562d2da8f1699cbezgif-83a731f8d738f3.jpg)

![7f8b3374980a49cc9749de5bc36e2047](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/2983c95760f941d7a11113b5305f38ed/images/7f8b3374980a49cc9749de5bc36e2047ezgif-82f1cb87a806ac.jpg)

![d26cda62305d4f2bb1929e31f4e53785](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/2983c95760f941d7a11113b5305f38ed/images/d26cda62305d4f2bb1929e31f4e53785ezgif-817f18418936ca.jpg)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202506/2983c95760f941d7a11113b5305f38ed/images/148553722077444cb64160621e698738Screenshot%20June%2018%202025%2011%3A35%3A10.png)
content_description: Showcasing Dollfication’s award-winning pastel '90s Gyaru-inspired fashion doll designs and creative process using Marvelous Designer and CLO.
